questions.q: What do `dbt docs generate` and `dbt docs serve` each do?
options: generate compiles the project's metadata into catalog.json; serve starts a local server hosting it as a browsable site
generate writes new column descriptions automatically; serve deploys the docs to production
They are the same command, aliased for convenience
generate runs all tests; serve runs all models
questions.explain: generate builds the catalog from existing project metadata, serve makes it browsable locally.

questions.q: Where do the descriptions and test results shown in the docs site actually come from?
options: Metadata already written in schema.yml files and results from the last dbt test run — nothing new to author
A separate documentation file that must be written from scratch
An AI-generated summary of each model
Power BI's own metadata layer
questions.explain: The docs reuse what's already in the project's schema.yml files and test history, rather than requiring new content.

questions.q: What does the lineage graph show for this chapter's new models?
options: raw_orders and raw_payments flowing into their staging models, into int_orders__joined (also fed by the customers mart), into fct_orders
Only fct_orders, with no upstream dependencies shown
A flat list of all models in the project with no connections
Only the Power BI pages, not the dbt models
questions.explain: The DAG view shows real nodes and edges matching Lesson 2's plan, made visible and clickable.

questions.q: What does a missing edge in the lineage graph where you expected one usually mean?
options: A `ref()` or `source()` call isn't wired up the way you think it is
The docs site has a rendering bug unrelated to the project
That model has too many tests attached
Nothing — missing edges are cosmetic and don't indicate a problem
questions.explain: The lineage graph is built directly from ref()/source() calls, so a missing edge reflects a real wiring gap in the SQL.

questions.q: Why document and test this model layer before Power BI connects to it?
options: So whoever builds the Finance and Ops pages can trust what the columns mean without re-deriving the pipeline or needing a conversation every time
Because Power BI refuses to connect to an undocumented dbt model
Because dbt docs are required for a model to be materialized
There's no real reason — it's just convention
questions.explain: Documentation and tests are what make a clean handoff to whoever builds the BI layer possible.
